Bug_Title: SIC: Deadly embrace of non-static inner class and thread local (SIC_THREADLOCAL_DEADLY_EMBRACE)
Bug_Details:
This class is an inner class, but should probably be a static inner class.
  As it is, there is a serious danger of a deadly embrace between the inner class
  and the thread local in the outer class. Because the inner class isn't static,
  it retains a reference to the outer class.
  If the thread local contains a reference to an instance of the inner
  class, the inner and outer instance will both be reachable
  and not eligible for garbage collection.
Bug_Explanation: A non-static inner class (InnerClass) is referenced by a ThreadLocal in the outer class (OuterClass). This can lead to a memory leak as the inner class holds a reference to the outer class, and the ThreadLocal holds a reference to the inner class.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered by creating a new instance of the InnerClass and setting it in the ThreadLocal of the OuterClass. This creates a circular reference between the OuterClass and the InnerClass, preventing both from being garbage collected, causing a memory leak.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results confirm the presence of the bug. The test code creates a new instance of the InnerClass and sets it in the ThreadLocal of the OuterClass. This creates a circular reference between the OuterClass and the InnerClass, preventing both from being garbage collected, causing a memory leak. This is exactly the scenario described in the bug information.
